name: Parsec
description: A popular ultra-low-latency streaming client built for gaming and professional 3D/video work — best-in-class raw performance on the free tier, but color fidelity, virtual displays, and most collaboration features are locked behind the paid Warp/Teams plans.

Wayland Unattended Access.comment: Hosting on Wayland graphical sessions is not supported architecturally.

Relay Server.comment: Uses STUN servers for initialization and NAT traversal to establish a direct P2P connection. The High Performance Relay (HPR) mechanism for forced traffic proxying and self-hosting your own relay is only available on the Enterprise plan.

Tailscale Support.comment: No native integration. It can automatically route UDP traffic over the Tailscale interface, but only if the VPN client is already installed on the OS.

Multi-Monitor Support.comment: The free version only lets you switch between screens. Simultaneous output to multiple monitors (Virtual Displays) is a Teams feature.

Drawing Tablet Support.comment: Pen pressure/tilt passthrough only works with a Warp/Teams subscription.

Gamepad Passthrough.comment: One of the best XInput gamepad emulation implementations on the market, ideal for gaming.

Microphone Passthrough.comment: Microphone passthrough from client to host is behind a paywall (Warp/Teams).

Adaptive Bitrate.comment: Very aggressive and effective bitrate adaptation to minimize latency.

V-Sync.comment: Has a built-in V-Sync toggle and flexible FPS capping matched to the client monitor's refresh rate.

Session Sharing.comment: Native support for multi-user connections for collaborative work or gaming is available for free.

Multi-User Sessions.comment: The engine is fundamentally designed to capture a single specific graphical session (display). Terminal-server-style operation is not supported at all.

Virtual Display.comment: Creating up to three virtual displays is implemented via a proprietary VDD driver, but locked behind the paid Warp or Teams subscriptions.

4:4:4 Chroma Subsampling.comment: Only available on the paid Warp or Teams subscriptions. The free version is hard-locked to 4:2:0.

Frame Rate (FPS).comment: A base 60 FPS is available for free, while higher frame rates (up to 240 FPS) require a paid Warp subscription.

Session Recording.comment: There is no built-in screen recording feature even on the paid tiers; third-party software (OBS, ShadowPlay) is required.

Pre-Login Access.comment: Available if Parsec is installed in Shared Mode (as a system service).

SSO / OIDC.comment: SAML/SSO integration is only available on the most expensive Parsec for Teams Enterprise plan.

2FA / MFA.comment: Two-factor authentication is available for free on any personal account.

Address Book.comment: Managing teams, groups, and company computers requires a Teams subscription.

Audit Logs.comment: Connection logging via the Guest Access API or the admin panel is only available in Teams.

Mass Deployment.comment: Scripted deployment using a service token is available for enterprise customers.

RBAC.comment: Role assignment (Admin, Member, Guest) is managed through the Teams console.

Privacy Mode (Black Screen).comment: Blanking the host's physical display is only available with a Warp or Teams subscription.

Remote Printing.comment: The tool is focused on graphics work; there is no virtual printer driver.

Generic USB Passthrough.comment: Advanced passthrough of arbitrary USB devices is implemented via VirtualHere integration and only available on Teams plans.

File Manager UI.comment: There is no dedicated file management interface. File transfer (paid version only) works via plain Drag & Drop.

Text Chat.comment: A built-in basic text chat is available through the in-session overlay during an active connection.

On-Screen Whiteboard.comment: No drawing or annotation tools are available.

Proxy Support.comment: The client uses a proprietary UDP protocol (BUD) and does not natively support routing through standard SOCKS5/HTTP proxies.

UAC Handling.comment: For full interaction and input delivery to the Windows secure desktop, the host app needs to be installed as a system service — otherwise UAC prompts may render as a black screen or block input.

Drag & Drop.comment: File transfer isn't supported at all on the free version; it's only available in Parsec for Teams.

Browser client.comment: A lightweight web client is available at web.parsec.app.

Headless mode.comment: Without a monitor, the free version requires an HDMI dummy plug. The Virtual Displays feature is Enterprise-only.

Windows: Host.comment: Parsec's reference platform. Maximum performance and direct integration with hardware video encoders (DXGI/NVFBC).

macOS: Host.comment: Works great with hardware acceleration on Apple Silicon (M1/M2/M3) processors.

Linux X11: Host.comment: Linux hosting is officially geared mainly toward proprietary NVIDIA drivers and specific distro configurations.

Linux Wayland: Host.comment: Parsec's architecture isn't adapted to Wayland capture protocols; hosting is only possible by switching the session back to X11.

iOS: Client.comment: There is no official native iPhone/iPad app.

Web Browser: Client.comment: The web client works, but has bitrate and hardware decoding limitations compared to the desktop app.

Free Tier.comment: Excellent performance with no session time limits, but hard technical restrictions: a single monitor only, and 4:2:0 chroma subsampling (text can look mushy).

Personal: Monthly.comment: Warp plan. Removes the technical restrictions: unlocks 4:4:4 mode, virtual displays, and graphics tablet pressure passthrough.

Team / Business: Monthly.comment: Teams plan. Billed per user (seat). Unlocks the admin console, RBAC roles, and advanced passthrough for complex USB devices.

Enterprise.comment: For large teams (typically 30+ users). Adds corporate SSO/SAML integration, the Audit API, and the ability to self-host your own Team Relay router.
